scope: Control: can our own merge path reproduce a published edit once the direction is taken from that edit?
screen: verification/harsh-suites-derived 10-row subset (probes/screen10.jsonl), kind refusal, temperature 0, cap 1024
serve_config: -c 8192 --parallel 4 --jinja --no-webui port 8134, one server at a time, RTX 3060 12GiB
runner: scripts/capability_wave.py --kinds refusal (deterministic refusal-check, zero judge calls)
direction: recovered from the oracle weight delta (largest-norm column of the rank-1 delta) by scripts/recover_oracle_axes.pt, merged with spanfit build --axes axes_attn --scale 1.35 --axis-space output
oracle_structure: the recovered direction is one shared unit vector across the 27 edited layers: pairwise mean|cos| 0.9940 (mean signed +0.0316, signs alternate), and per layer the attention and MLP directions agree at mean|cos| 0.9958, at strength 1.29-1.45 per tensor
conclusion: converter, requantization and serve path are faithful; every earlier 0/10 with a fitted axis is a direction-discovery failure, not a write-path failure
not_a_claim: the direction here came from the published edit, so this is an instrument control and not an independent result
